samples.summary: The CLI-side nonce check — the central new behavior of this delta — has no test at all
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer`/`stateMatches` in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:168-214 add the guard that rejects a `/callback?code=…` lacking this invocation's nonce (400 'State mismatch', without settling the promise). Nothing exercises it: neither helper is exported, `registerLoginCommand` is only wired in packages/cli/src/cli.ts, and no file under packages/cli/test references login, /callback, state matching or 'State mismatch'. The only tests added in this delta are packages/cli/test/url.test.ts (about `seg`) and one backend controller test for the redirect. So the CLI could stop enforcing the nonce (e.g. accept a null state, or compare the wrong field) and the green suite would say nothing — this is precisely the fake-coverage shape: the security fix is described in comments and asserted only on the backend half.

samples.summary: New CLI_STATE_PATTERN validation in GitHubAuthGuard is untested — no guard spec exists
samples.evidence: This delta adds `CLI_STATE_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/` and the `typeof cliState === 'string' && test(...) ? cliState : undefined` branch (github-auth.guard.ts:18, 31-38). There is no `github-auth.guard.spec.ts`: `packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts` contains only auth.controller, jwt.strategy, github.strategy, cli-auth.store and auth.service specs. So neither the accept path (a real 43-char base64url nonce stored on the state), the reject path (malformed/array/absent cliState → stored as undefined), nor the boundary lengths are covered. A pattern that silently rejected the CLI's real nonce format would ship green and break every `wafflebase login` with 'State mismatch'.

samples.summary: The no-nonce branch of the redirect is not asserted: the pre-existing regex is unanchored and passes either way
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts:130-135 now has two branches: append `&state=<nonce>` or append nothing. The new test (spec:221-238) covers the first with an anchored `$` regex. The second is only 'covered' by the older test at spec:192-206, whose matcher `/^http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:9876\/callback\?code=.+/` is unanchored, so it passes whether or not a `&state=` is appended — it cannot detect the new branch leaking a stale/undefined nonce (e.g. `&state=undefined`). No test asserts the redirect ends at the code when no nonce was stored.

samples.summary: CliAuthStore's new cliState field has no round-trip test; the existing toEqual silently tolerates it
samples.evidence: createState/consumeState gained a `cliState` field (cli-auth.store.ts:30-59) but cli-auth.store.spec.ts still only calls `createState('browser', 9876)` and asserts `toEqual({ csrf, mode, port })` (line 35) — jest `toEqual` ignores an extra `cliState: undefined`, so that assertion holds whether or not the field is stored or returned. No test stores a nonce and reads it back, or checks it is scoped per state token.

samples.summary: New controller test uses a fixture nonce ('nonce-abc') that the guard's own validator would reject, so it does not represent a real flow
samples.evidence: The test mints the state with `cliAuthStore.createState('cli', 9876, 'nonce-abc')`. 'nonce-abc' is 9 characters and would fail GitHubAuthGuard's `CLI_STATE_PATTERN` (16-128 chars), and the real CLI nonce is a 43-char base64url string (login.ts:40). The assertion also uses a nonce with no characters that `encodeURIComponent` alters, so the encoding step in auth.controller.ts:131 is never exercised. The test still verifies the echo, so this is a fixture-realism point rather than vacuity.

verdict.reason: Verified the code: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:40-46 mints a per-invocation nonce and passes it to startCallbackServer; login.ts:168-173 defines stateMatches (non-exported, null-rejecting, timingSafeEqual); login.ts:206-214 rejects a /callback whose state does not match with 400 'State mismatch' and does not settle the promise. Searched wide for any test exercising this and found none: repo-wide grep for 'State mismatch|stateMatches|startCallbackServer' matches only login.ts, docs/design/cli.md, and an unrelated slides thumbnail-panel.ts; repo-wide grep for 'cliState|callbackServer|/callback' hits only backend source/specs, docs, and packages/backend/test/helpers/integration-helpers.ts:93-94 (a GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL env default, not a CLI test). All 28 files under packages/cli/test/** were listed; none is a login/auth test, and a grep of test imports shows tests import root/tabs/docs/cells/notes/slides/files/api-keys/sheets/schema/ctx but never ../src/commands/login.js — the only importer is packages/cli/src/cli.ts:10. packages/cli/test/bin.test.ts has no login/spawn usage, and scripts/agent/auth-smoke.test.mjs is about Claude Code login errors, unrelated. Both helpers being unexported means the guard is unreachable from a unit test as written. This is the 'missing test' shape in my lane: a real behavior change (nonce enforcement on the loopback callback) with no meaningful test; the CLI could accept a null state or compare the wrong field and the suite would stay green, since only the backend half is asserted.

mergedFrom.summary: New module `url.ts` has no direct unit test; `seg('')` empty-segment rejection and the server trailing-slash normalisation are untested

finding.summary: New empty-segment rejection in `seg()` has no test, and it is the branch most likely to fire in normal use (unconfigured workspace defaults to `''`)
finding.evidence: `seg()` now throws for `encoded === ''` (url.ts:33). `resolveConfig` defaults `workspace` to `''` in all four branches (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:100,126,147,164) and config.test.ts:30 asserts that default, so with no workspace configured every command (live and --dry-run) now throws `Invalid identifier ""` instead of the previously-documented `/workspaces//...` 404 path (comment at config.ts:108 and config.test.ts:101-104 still describe that old behaviour). No test exercises the empty case: the new suites only cover `..` (http-client-paths.test.ts:131-159, read-dry-run.test.ts:299-320). The new behaviour and the new user-facing error message for the most common misconfiguration ship untested.

verdict.reason: Both halves of the finding fail against the repository. (1) The claimed behavior does not exist: `seg()` rejects only dot segments via `DOT_SEGMENT = /^(?:\.|%2e){1,2}$/i` (url.ts:13), which cannot match the empty string, so `seg('')` returns `''` (url.ts:39-48). The doc comment at url.ts:31-37 states explicitly that the empty segment is deliberately NOT rejected, precisely so an unconfigured workspace does not break every command and every --dry-run preview — so the `config.ts:108` `/workspaces//...` 404 comment is still accurate, not stale. (2) Even read as a pure coverage claim, the empty case is directly and non-vacuously tested in `packages/cli/test/url.test.ts`, a file the reviewer's glob reported as non-existent: url.test.ts:38-40 asserts `seg('') === ''`; url.test.ts:56-60 asserts `apiV1Base` with `workspace: ''` yields `https://api.example.test/api/v1/workspaces/`; url.test.ts:92-96 asserts `apiKeysUrl` with `workspace: ''` yields `https://api.example.test/workspaces//api-keys`. Each pins an exact output string that would fail if `seg()` started throwing on or altering the empty segment. The suite is executed: vitest.config.ts:5 includes `test/**/*.test.ts`. The dot-segment rejection that does exist is also covered (url.test.ts:24-28, 62-66, 85-90).
